confirmed_source_facts.fact: read_joystick stores each non-neutral cardinal request into JOY_DIR, PLAYER_WANT, PLAYER_FACE before collision. Main pt_try_late_turn calls can_move; rejection branches to pt_draw, holding position and step while facing reflects the request.

Both shared-text name_tick variants call name_late_turn. When name_can_move rejects a perpendicular request during a partial cell, the helper returns A=0; the tick interprets zero as continue and advances the existing PLAYER_DIR. The cursor therefore advances on the old trajectory while the main player holds. This is a confirmed source-level behavioral mismatch.

Reversal and admitted perpendicular turns use inverse counters: PLAYER_STEP is elapsed 0..3; PRES_NAME_STEPS at $DE is remaining 4..1. Both reverse by complementing the counter and rebasing PLAYER_CELL; admitted turns store elapsed progress in TURN_SNAP and perform two-axis correction per movement tick. Static source structure is equivalent under that mapping; runtime equivalence is not measured.

Manual neutral input is checked before pending snap processing in both paths; position/snap and buffered direction are retained. Name redraws; main marks the player render. Main samples after render, while name samples inside name_tick, so exact input/render phase differs.

At aligned start, main clears PLAYER_DIR after a blocked request; name remains idle but leaves the prior PLAYER_DIR value. Since name step is zero, no movement results and the next legal start overwrites it. No user-visible consequence is established; it is a hidden state mismatch if strict state-level parity is required.

DIR_N/E/S/W are 0/1/2/3. Main regular-cell can_move tests the target reciprocal entrance bit. Name tests current outgoing bits 1/2/4/8. Generator blocks authored wall/perimeter/top-right anchor cells and clears both sides of every adjacent blocked edge, so ordinary remaining edges are reciprocal. Static edge-bit semantics align; name geometry has no rotating-gate owner.
